overview: Medieval Krakow linked royal power, urban government, commerce and religious communities within the wider Polish kingdom.

items.text: Krakow received its charter in 1257. Its planned streets and plots remain legible in the historic city.
Kazimierz, chartered in 1335, was a separate medieval town; its history includes Catholic and Jewish communities.
Wawel Hill contained a royal residence and burial complex.
Krakow became an important administrative and commercial centre where crafts and learning developed. Later monuments must be dated separately from this medieval chapter.
